extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of art history, critics, and those studying Renaissance painting and sculpture
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for interpreting and judging fifteenth-century Italian painting and sculpture (style, expression, technique, symbolism, and cultural position). Useful to art historians, critics, and students assessing works by artists like Botticelli and Luca della Robbia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the unique quality or 'peculiar sensation' of a work
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the peculiar sensation, what is the peculiar quality of pleasure, which his work has the property of exciting in us, and which we cannot get elsewhere?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critic's chief question is to answer this: isolate the singular affective or aesthetic quality that distinguishes an artist (e.g., Botticelli's particular charm). Support with examples from the work (recurrent types, mood, imagery) rather than generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend of narrative (poetry) and formal means (line and colour) — the 'poetical painter'
rubrics_metrics.description: He is before all things a poetical painter, blending the charm of story and sentiment, the medium of the art of poetry, with the charm of line and colour, the medium of abstract painting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how an artist integrates narrative content and poetic feeling with formal pictorial elements. Look for illustrative engagement with literature (e.g., Dante) and how line and colour carry sentiment beyond literal story-telling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original painter's vision versus literal translation
rubrics_metrics.description: The design is no mere translation of Dante's words, but a true painter's vision; illustrations crowded with incident yet showing invention rather than literal transcription.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether imagery transcends literal source-text illustration—does the artist invent pictorial solutions, combine phases of a scene imaginatively, and create novel visual metaphors rather than simply copy verbal description?

rubrics_metrics.name: Visionary reworking of observed reality (selective combination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The genius usurps the data before it as the exponent of ideas, moods, visions of its own; it plays fast and loose with those data, rejecting some and isolating others, and always combining them anew.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge how an artist transforms observed details to express an inner mood or idea: selective omission, recombination, and emphasis signal visionary power. Note departures from naturalistic transcription as positive devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional sympathy and moral stance (middle world sympathy)
rubrics_metrics.description: His morality is all sympathy; he accepts that middle world in which men take no side in great conflicts, and decide no great causes... his interest is neither in untempered goodness nor untempered evil, but in men and women in their mixed and uncertain condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the work's moral/emotional posture: does it sympathise with ambiguous human states rather than moral extremes? Consider how sentiment of wistfulness, exile, or melancholy is conveyed and whether that constitutes the artist's ethical temperament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of type and expressive formal choices (lighting, colour, pose)
rubrics_metrics.description: He has worked out in them a distinct and peculiar type, definite enough in his own mind, for he has painted it over and over again... The white light on it is cast up hard and cheerless from below... the child's gaze is always far from her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recurring 'types' (e.g., Botticelli's Madonnas) and how formal choices—lighting direction, tonal palette, facial types, gestures—produce a specific emotional effect. Repetition of type can be a deliberate expressive strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative colouring as expressive spirit rather than naturalism
rubrics_metrics.description: All colour is no mere delightful quality of natural things, but a spirit upon them by which they become expressive to the spirit... his predilection for minor tones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge colour not only for naturalistic fidelity but for its imaginative, expressive function. Minor tones or subdued palettes may deliberately convey mood; critique should analyse colour as symbolic or emotive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis of classical subject matter with contemporary sentiment and stylistic devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Classical story was regarded as so much imaginative material to be received and assimilated... in Botticelli's Venus the grotesque emblems of the middle age, and a landscape full of its peculiar feeling, frame a figure that reminds you of the faultless nude studies of Ingres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how classical myths are reinterpreted through the period's stylistic vocabulary (medieval emblems, Gothic drapery, contemporary landscape). Consider coherence between subject and the anachronistic or hybrid visual language used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technique (low relief) to etherealise form and avoid hard realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Their sculpture shares... that profound expressiveness... Their works have... low relief, giving even to their monumental effigies something of its depression of surface, getting into them by this means a pathetic suggestion of the wasting and etherealisation of death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In sculpture, assess the choice of relief depth and modelling as expressive devices: low relief can subdue mass, suggest ethereality or decay, and avoid 'hard realism.' Analyse how surface treatment serves emotional ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of heaviness and emphasis in favour of subtle shadow and delicate expression
rubrics_metrics.description: They are haters of all heaviness and emphasis, of strongly-opposed light and shade, and seek their means of expression among those last refinements of shadow... The whole essence of their work is EXPRESSION, the passing of a smile over the face of a child, the ripple of the air on a still day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value subtle gradations and minimal modelling as deliberate expressive choices. Critique should note restraint, fine shadowing, and small gestures as the core communicative elements rather than dramatic chiaroscuro.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allgemeinheit (universality) — abstracting the type from the individual
rubrics_metrics.description: Allgemeinheit—breadth, generality, universality... which prompted [Greek sculptors] constantly to seek the type in the individual, to abstract and express only what is structural and permanent, to purge from the individual all that belongs only to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the work aspires to universal types by abstracting idiosyncratic detail. Such abstraction produces a 'breadth of humanity' and enduring cultural resonance; critique should weigh this against loss of individuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance universality and individual expression; deliberate incompleteness as effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Michelangelo... secured for his work individuality and intensity of expression, while he avoided a too hard realism... leaving nearly all his sculpture in a puzzling sort of incompleteness... that incompleteness is Michelangelo's equivalent for colour in sculpture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate strategies that reconcile type and individuality: studied incompleteness, partial finish, and selective emphasis can suggest life and inwardness. See incompleteness as an intentional aesthetic device, not a flaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis of systems (midway approaches combining Greek and Michelangelesque methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Midway between these two systems—the system of the Greek sculptors and the system of Michelangelo—comes the system of Luca della Robbia... they unite elements of tranquillity, of repose, to that intense and individual expression by a system of conventionalism... throwing the whole into lower relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify artists who synthesize opposing traditions (universality vs individual intensity). Critique should articulate how conventionalisation, relief depth, and compositional restraint merge to produce a distinctive balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of material, context, and site to a work's charm
rubrics_metrics.description: No work is less imitable; like Tuscan wine, it loses its savour when moved from its birthplace, from the crumbling walls where it was first placed... he became desirous to realise the spirit and manner of that sculpture, in a humbler material, to unite its science... to adorn and cultivate daily household life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how material (marble, pottery, glazed earthenware) and original setting contribute to meaning and effect. Consider site-specificity and how relocation or change of material can diminish intended qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sculptural equivalents for colour and the inadvisability of mere colour as remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of colour in sculpture is but an unskilful contrivance to effect, by borrowing from another art, what the nobler sculpture effects by strictly appropriate means... To get not colour, but the equivalent of colour; to secure the expression and the play of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When critiquing sculpture, prefer formal/structural means (modelling, surface, incompleteness, relief) to colour as expressive tools. If colour is used, examine whether it supplants or complements sculptural technique.
